item.description: Local volunteer attorneys offer free legal information and referral for matters of family law only. These lawyer consultations will last up to 20 minutes. Sign-ups are first come, first served in person and begin at 10 am. \(30 minutes before the program begins\) The attorneys are volunteers and provide only legal information. They do not provide specific legal advice and should not be considered as personal lawyers for any reason. You will be required to sign a waiver before speaking to an attorney that states that no attorney-client relationship is being created with this free service. No language translation services or interpreters are offered or provided by library staff. Participants must bring their own interpreter if one is needed. Participants may also bring support persons, family members or other affiliated persons to meet with the attorney together. item.title: Marin Farmers Markets — Thu Sep 10, 8:00 AM — Marin Veterans' Memorial Auditorium
item.description:
Price: Free
Sponsor: Marin Center
Explore the bounty of summer at the Marin Farmers Markets. Taste vine-ripened tomatoes, corn that was picked that morning, and peaches so juicy you have to bend over just to get a bite. Farm-fresh eggs, grass-fed beef, artisan c heeses, raw milk, and freshly baked breads complete the shopping exper ience. Specialty prepared foods and handmade art add to the magic of the market.
Enjoy the intimate feeling of the Thursday Marin Farmers Market, an ideal place to meet for lunch and pick up fresh produce for the weekend. Discover the abundance and diversity of product at the celebrated Sunday Marin Farmers Market, the third largest farmers market in California. Turn your dollar into a vote for local sustainable agriculture, shrink your eco-footprint, and revive the feeling of being intimate ly connected to your food by meeting your farmers face-to-face. The market takes place rain or shine.
www.aginstitutemarin.org
Source: North Bay Bohemian, Press Dem

item.title: Death Medicine presented by the Luminous Threshold Collective — Thu Sep 10, 7:00 PM — The Lost Church
item.description:
**$15 General Admission**
**Doors at 6:30pm.**
**Show from 7:00-9:00pm with one intermission**
Bring your songs, poetry, stories, dance or any other expression your heart feels called to offer around the topics of death and grief. We are the Luminous Threshold Collective. We are called end of life doulas, death midwives, deathcare workers, deathwalkers or deathtenders. We collaborate with the dying and those close to them on every facet of their journey toward and through the portal between this life and the next. We want to increase community building, support and engagement around the topics of death, dying, grief and loss and, in so doing, heighten everyone’s moment to moment awareness of the beauty and preciousness of the gift of life. The event will be an open mic format where people can sing, dance, recite poetry, or speak extemporaneously about their experiences of death and grief and be witnessed and heard by a radically present and loving audience in a well-held container.

item.title: Dream Counselor Cohort — Fri Sep 11, 10:00 AM — Online
item.description:
Guiding undocumented students isn't simple. It takes care. It takes clarity. And it matters, because every student, no matter their status, deserves a strong foundation for the future. California believes in that future. For all our students. Our state works to make college accessible and worth it for undocumented students. That's where you come in. For undocumented students, the path through college is shaped by barriers most never see. These barriers show up in the questions students are afraid to ask, the forms leave blank, the doors they never try to open. This workshop changes that! Register to connect with counselors from across California. You'll build strategies that help immigrant families prepare for college, and look ahead through tough times. Audience: High School and College CounselorsTo register visit the SRJC Undocu Immigrant Dream Center website. (https://dream.santarosa.edu/workshops-events-2026-2027)

item.title: Frank Lloyd Wright Civic Center Tours — Fri Sep 11, 10:30 AM — Civic Center
item.description:
Price: Adult $10, Senior/Full Time Student $5 \(Plus a $2 p er ticket service Charge Online\)
Ticket Info:
Sponsor: Marin Center
Link: http://www.marincounty.org/depts/cu
The Frank Lloyd Wright-designed Marin County Civic Center is a national- and state-designated historic landmark. item.title: Guided Nature Walk & Ranch House tour Anderson Marsh — Sat Sep 12, 8:30 AM — Anderson Marsh State Historic Park
item.description:
The next “Second Saturday” Guided Nature walk at Anderson Marsh State Historic Park will be held on Saturday, September 12, 2026.
The Guided Walk will begin at 8:30am. Bring binoculars and meet in the parking lot at 8:15am for an opportunity to observe the birds and other wildlife found in the picnic area. Sturdy shoes, a hat and water are suggested.
The September guided walk will be led by State Parks volunteer docent Roberta Lyons and will provide an opportunity to observe wildlife at the park and learn about their natural habitat, as well as to learn about the natural and cultural history of the area.
The walk will take between 1½ and 2 hours, depending on the route taken. Dogs are not allowed on the park trails.
A tour of the historic Anderson Ranch House will be available immediately after the conclusion of the walk.
There is no charge for the Nature Walk and Ranch House tour and parking is free for those attending.
Source: Press Democrat
